_meta.indication: ENJAYMO is indicated to decrease the need for red blood cell (RBC) transfusion due to hemolysis in adults with cold agglutinin disease (CAD).

pivotal_trials.population: Adults (>=18 years) with primary CAD, chronic hemolysis, hemoglobin <=10 g/dL, symptomatic disease, and at least one blood transfusion in the 6 months prior to enrollment
pivotal_trials.endpoint: Composite responder rate: no blood transfusion from Week 5 through Week 26, no prohibited CAD medication, and Hgb >=12 g/dL or increase of >=2 g/dL from baseline at the treatment assessment timepoint
pivotal_trials.result: 13 of 24 patients (54.2%, 95% CI 32.8, 74.4) met the composite responder criteria, with the lower bound of the 95% CI >30%; components: 15 (62.5%) met the Hgb endpoint, 17 (70.8%) transfusion-free Weeks 5-26, 22 (91.7%) received no prohibited CAD medications

key_safety: Most common adverse reactions (>=10%): respiratory tract infection, viral infection, diarrhea, dyspepsia, cough, arthralgia, arthritis, and peripheral edema. Serious infections (including encapsulated bacteria) reported in 17% (4/24); serious adverse reactions in 13% (3/24). Infusion-related reactions in 2 of 24 patients (8%).
target_moa: Humanized IgG4 monoclonal antibody that inhibits the classical complement pathway by binding C1s, a serine protease that cleaves C4; inhibition at the level of C1s prevents complement deposition on RBCs, resulting in inhibition of hemolysis in CAD

advisory_committee.vote: No advisory committee was convened; the application did not raise significant public health questions and provided substantial evidence of effectiveness with no critical safety issues
